historicalVersion.note: Search implementation returns active records only; historical retrieval queries are retained as approved and scored without changing their expected labels.

implementationLimitations: The SQLite provider uses lexical substring matching over content, requires all selected query terms in order, and takes at most the first five terms longer than two characters; it does not interpret natural-language filters or semantic paraphrases.
The provider search path filters to active records, so superseded R1 is not available through normal searches even when a query requests history.
Q10 and Q11 are executed verbatim. Separate matching-term controls test restricted-memory exclusion/inclusion because the exact natural-language queries may not lexically match R7.
Category/type fields are passed as explicit provider filters for Q08 and Q09, as indicated by those exact query phrases; the text itself is not parsed by the SQLite provider.
This fixed synthetic set is not evidence of production-corpus representativeness. No ranking, schema, or production-memory changes were made.
